$comment: STORAGE SIZE PROFILES — the per-deployment ladder for `longhorn` PVC capacity.
Read by src/Core.TypeScript/cluster/storage-profiles.ts, which the
single-node readiness auditor imports. Applied to the manifests by
`bun src/Core.TypeScript/cluster/storage-profiles.ts --profile <name> --apply`.
Aaron 2026-08-20: 'until we have some other formatting we should try to take
up all storage with PVCs, we also need a minimal size. We should not over
provision. Some of our boxes are NASs some are regular PCs.'
Four constraints, and they pull against each other:
(a) never declare more than the node's real disk        HARD
(b) a minimum that fits a 200-300 GiB box
(c) on a bigger box, use the storage rather than idle it
(d) heterogeneous hardware, so it is a per-deployment choice
(c) CANNOT be satisfied by elasticity today, and this file does not pretend
otherwise. Growing a PVC after the fact needs `allowVolumeExpansion` plus a
filesystem grow, and SHRINKING a PVC is not supported by Kubernetes at all —
the only way down is destroy-and-restore. So a volume sized for a big box can
never be moved to a small one, which makes 'size it big and shrink later' a
one-way door. A ladder chosen ONCE at bring-up is the honest mechanism until
a resize path exists. See docs in storage-profiles.ts §WHAT THIS IS NOT.
== THE ARITHMETIC A PROFILE HAS TO SURVIVE ==============================
Longhorn does not make a node's whole disk schedulable. Two settings bound it,
both left at chart defaults by applications/longhorn/Application.yaml:
storageMinimalAvailablePercentage   default 25   (longhorn-1.7.2/values.yaml
line ~216: 'The default
value is 25')
storageOverProvisioningPercentage   default 100  (same file, line ~214)
so schedulable ~= 0.75 x (disk - OS root). A profile total T therefore needs a
box of roughly  T / 0.75 + ~30 GiB of root  before Longhorn will place it:
minimal    200 GiB declared  ->  ~267 GiB Longhorn disk  ->  a ~300 GiB box
standard   595 GiB declared  ->  ~793 GiB Longhorn disk  ->  a ~850 GiB box
measured   967 GiB declared  ->  ~1289 GiB Longhorn disk ->  see below
large     1599 GiB declared  ->  ~2132 GiB Longhorn disk ->  a ~2.2 TiB box
`measured` is the rung this deployment runs, and the row above is the
misleading way to read it, which is why the auditor prints two numbers per
rung and not one. Applying T/0.75 to a DECLARED total prices in capacity
that no fresh sync provisions. `measured` provisions 467 GiB at bring-up,
so it stands up on a ~653 GiB box; the ~1289 figure is what it would need
if every Application in this catalogue were synced, which includes 500 GiB
of model-cache ceiling that nothing applies today. Both are true, neither
is a discount on the other, and both are printed.
HONEST LIMIT, stated because a profile that quietly does not fit is worse than
a red gate: `minimal` fits a 300 GiB box, NOT a 200 GiB one. A 200 GiB disk
has only ~127 GiB schedulable after the same arithmetic. The auditor does this
sum against MEASURED node capacity, so nobody has to trust this paragraph.
The active profile is NOT set here. It is `activeStorageProfile` in
full-ai-cluster/k8s/single-node-budget.json, beside nodeCount and the
acknowledgements, because it is a property of THIS deployment and the ledger
is already the deployment's checked-in record. This file is the catalogue.
== POD COUNTS ARE PART OF THE FOOTPRINT, AND ONE OF THEM IS A TRAP =======
A claim's cost is size x POD COUNT, and the pod count is not always in the
manifest. Each row therefore records `podsSource`:
manifest       a scalar in this repo governs it; `podsField` names it, and
the auditor cross-checks the manifest against `pods` here.
chart-default  the upstream chart decides. `podsEvidence` must cite chart,
version and the values path. The auditor CANNOT derive these
by reading our YAML, so this file is the only place they are
written down.
singleton      the component runs exactly one pod by construction.
MEASURED 2026-08-21, and this is why the field exists: the readiness auditor's
own extractor derived mimir at 150 GiB. mimir-distributed 5.5.1 ships
`ingester.replicas: 3` and `ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled: true` over
three zones, and templates/_helpers.tpl line 568 computes
`replicaPerZone = ceil(replicas / zones)` — so ingester renders 1 pod in each
of 3 zone StatefulSets = 3 PVCs, and store_gateway (replicas: 1, also
zone-aware) renders ceil(1/3) = 1 per zone = 3 PVCs too. Real mimir footprint
is 350 GiB, not 150. A 200 GiB under-count, in the direction that fills a disk.
The opposite error was there too: the extractor's nearest-enclosing-replicas
heuristic gave redis MASTER the `replica.replicaCount: 2` next door, counting
10 GiB that does not exist (bitnami redis `architecture: replication` runs
exactly one master). +200 and -10 against a derived 1409 is how 1599 is the
true total.
== A NUMBER WITHOUT ITS GOVERNOR IS NOT A SIZE ==========================
`prometheus: 100Gi` means nothing without a retention bound beside it. Cut
the volume, leave the governor where it was, and you have not made the
footprint smaller — you have made an eviction loop. So a row may declare
`governors`: non-capacity scalars, per profile, written and verified in the
SAME --apply pass as the size they bound. They cannot land in separate
commits and they cannot drift, because verifyProfileApplied checks them
exactly like sizes. `governorEvidence` is required and non-empty, for the
same reason `podsEvidence` is: a bound with no stated origin is a number
somebody picked and nothing can tell that from a requirement.
The one row that has governors today is prometheus. Its old `consequence`
asked whoever selected a smaller rung to remember to cut retention by hand.
An instruction to remember is the vacuity class — it reads like a guard and
constrains nothing — and replacing it with a mechanism is what this field
is for.
AN EMPTY `governors` IS A REAL ANSWER, not an omission, and the rows say
which case they are in:
moves by itself   nats. Chart 1.2.7 emits `max_file_store: {{ pvc.size }}`
when fileStore.maxSize is unset (files/config/
jetstream.yaml:17), so the server limit tracks the PVC.
no history to     mimir ingester / store-gateway / compactor. Working
govern            space; the blocks live in object storage.
no mechanism      weaviate, cockroachdb, hindsight postgres, agent-memory.
exists            They refuse writes when full. There is no scalar to turn
and the row says so instead of implying one.
DOES NOT move,    tempo. The chart default `tempo.retention: 24h`
and is left       (values.yaml:57 -> compactor block_retention) is a TIME
window that cannot see the disk, so shrinking the volume
does not shorten it. Cutting it would need a measured
span rate nobody here has, and inventing one and calling
it a requirement is the thing this file exists to stop.
The residual risk is named in the manifest instead.
== SCHEDULED AT BRING-UP vs DECLARED ====================================
`scheduledAtBringUp: false` means no PVC object is created on a fresh sync, so
the capacity is planning-only. It is NOT a discount on the hard constraint:
the moment a maintainer syncs the app, the full size lands. Longhorn's
StorageClass is `volumeBindingMode: Immediate` (hardcoded at
longhorn-1.7.2/templates/storageclass.yaml line 18, not configurable), so an
applied PVC provisions its replica with ZERO consuming pods — `replicas: 0` on
the workload buys nothing. What buys it is the Application never being applied.
So the auditor convicts on DECLARED and merely REPORTS bring-up. A gate that
convicted on the bring-up subset would pass today and fail the first time
someone ran `argocd app sync ollama`, which is a check that did not run
wearing the face of one that passed.

== A REQUEST IS A RESERVATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT ========================
Cutting a request below the app's real working set does not make the app smaller.
Without a matching limit it makes the pod more over-committed, and moves the
failure from a Pending pod (loud, scheduler-attributed) to the kernel OOM killer
(quiet, arbitrary). So every row that cuts has to say what the cut costs, and the
loader refuses one that does not.
AND THE SUM IS A FLOOR, NOT THE REQUIREMENT. 28 of the 45 Applications render
pods that request NOTHING (`resources: {}` chart defaults). Those pods are
BestEffort: the scheduler admits any number of them and no arithmetic here ever
sees them. The envelope's unreserved headroom is what they actually run in.
== DISK IS THE TIGHTER CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS NOT PVCs ===================
MEASURED 2026-08-21 by reading each rendered image's registry manifest and summing
its layer sizes, then measuring the compressed:uncompressed ratio by streaming and
gunzipping four of them (argocd v2.13.2 x2.69, loki 3.3.2 x3.21, kube-state-metrics
v2.14.0 x3.39, cockroach v24.2.4 x2.49 -- aggregate x2.67; containerd stores layers
UNCOMPRESSED, so that is the multiplier that matters):
cohort         distinct images   compressed   on disk at x2.67
asserted 19                 39      1.61 GB           ~4.3 GB
applied 33                  73     11.77 GB          ~31 GB
Against the runner disk -- and THE RUNNER DISK IS NOT 14 GB. MEASURED 2026-08-22
on run 32585090483 by `runner-disk.ts --measure`, after checkout and toolchain
install, on BOTH hosted runners this lane uses:
ubuntu-24.04       /  144.26 GiB total, 67.18 used,  77.06 GiB AVAILABLE
ubuntu-24.04-arm   /  144.26 GiB total, 45.23 used,  99.02 GiB AVAILABLE
There is ONE filesystem; neither runner has a second disk at /mnt, and `docker
info` puts images on /var/lib/docker, which is on /. So the 14 GB this file
divided by is a vendor figure describing no machine this lane runs on, and the
'2.2x over / 5.5x over' verdicts computed from it were wrong in the direction
that under-reports what fits.
AND THE UNITS HAVE TO BE SAID OUT LOUD, because this is exactly where they
bite: registry sizes are DECIMAL GB, `df` and freeDiskGib are BINARY GiB.
77.06 GiB available is 82.74 GB decimal. So against the MEASURED x64 runner:
asserted 33   ~8.2 GB   fits, 10x over
applied  37  ~34.3 GB   fits, 2.4x over
all      46  ~79.7 GB   FITS -- by ~3 GB, on a 96%-full disk
and on the arm runner (99.02 GiB = 106.3 GB) all 46 fits with 25% to spare.
THE DECLARED BOUND IS STILL 14 AND THAT IS ON PURPOSE -- see
`measuredFreeDiskGib`. `image-footprint.ts --report` therefore prints TWO
verdicts per cohort, against the declared budget and against the measurement,
and they disagree loudly. That disagreement is the state of the tree, not a
bug in either number.
AND THE x2.67 ESTIMATE IS ITSELF HIGH FOR THE TWO IMAGES THAT DECIDE THIS,
measured on run 32588276375 by PULLING them on a hosted ubuntu-24.04 rather
than multiplying:
image                    compressed   est x2.67   ACTUAL extracted   ratio
hindsight-api 0.1.1         8.81 GB    23.51 GB           15.58 GB   x1.77
vllm-openai   latest        9.11 GB    24.33 GB           21.42 GB   x2.35
So hindsight costs ~14.5 GiB, not ~23 GB, and the runner SURVIVED BOTH: 85.73
GiB free at job start, 50.05 GiB free after hindsight, its postgres and
control-plane closure, AND vllm -- 35.68 GiB in total, 176s and 172s to pull.
Neither image is self-hosted-only on disk. The ratio stays 2.67 in this file
because that is the only figure measured across a SPREAD of images; the two
rows above are what a real pull says about the two that dominate, and the
disagreement is recorded rather than resolved by picking the flattering one.
A further 20.72 GiB (x64) / 4.52 GiB (arm) sits in preinstalled toolchains no
k8s lane invokes -- android 10.81, ghcup 3.66, swift 3.29, CodeQL 1.69,
powershell 1.27 -- measured in the same run. `runner-disk.ts --reclaim` deletes
exactly that named set and re-measures. Nothing runs it today, because nothing
needs to yet, and it costs wall clock on every run that does.
THE PER-APP BREAKDOWN these totals never carried is `image-footprint.ts
--report`. The top 5 apps are 83.7% of the bytes and FOUR of them are already
glob-excluded from the dev lane: vllm/vllm-openai:latest at 9.11 GB compressed
(excluded) and ghcr.io/vectorize-io/hindsight-api:0.1.1 at 8.81 GB (~23 GB
unpacked) are most of it, and only hindsight is APPLIED. No rung in this file
changes either: a CPU/memory ladder cannot shrink an image.
What CAN, for hindsight: upstream publishes 0.5.1 at 1.38 GB and 0.5.1-slim at
0.69 GB -- 12x smaller than the pinned 0.1.1 -- and there is no slim variant AT
the pin (the -slim tags begin at 0.5.1). Chart 0.3.0 does read `api.image.tag`,
VERIFIED in the render: --set api.image.tag=0.5.1-slim moves the rendered image
and nothing else. Whether app 0.5.x runs under chart 0.3.0's templates is
UNTESTED, so this is a named option, not a recommendation.
Honest limit, same kind and a different count: 15 of the 126 images could not be
sized -- 4 private ghcr.io/lucent-financial-group, 2 private ghcr.io/flowdent, 8
bitnami/ich777 tags withdrawn upstream (404), 1 rate-limited (429). They are
counted in no total above and they are NOT zero.
AND THE PVC NUMBERS ONE LADDER UP DO NOT APPLY HERE. On kind the storage class is
local-path, which is a hostPath directory with NO quota: a PVC request reserves
nothing and consumes nothing until something writes. So a storage-heavy set can
look like it fits and then fill the disk under load. The GiB in this file's
storage ladder are scheduling reservations on Longhorn; on the runner they are not
bytes at all.
requestsField  dotted path of the `requests` MAP; `.cpu` and `.memory` hang off it
pods           how many pods this ONE value is multiplied by
metalSource    manifest    our own valuesObject already sets it
chart-default  the upstream chart decides; `evidence` must cite
chart, version and values path, because no reader
of our YAML can find it otherwise
cpuMillis 0    NOT a missing value. It means the container declares no CPU
reservation, which is what most chart defaults do, and the
verifier reads it as 'this key must be ABSENT'.
HONEST LIMIT ON THE COVERAGE CHECK: it enumerates DEPTH-1 directories, i.e. the
45 `applications/<dir>/Application.yaml` files. ArgoCD's include glob is not
path-segment bounded, so the root ALSO applies
`applications/game-hosting/gmod/Application.yaml` -- a 46th Application this
check cannot see. It contributes 0m / 0Mi today (in-repo manifests, no requests,
and it fails its sync on every reconcile against gatekeeper's webhook), so no
total above is wrong. What is not guarded HERE is a FUTURE nested Application
that does request something. That case is already caught one check over:
app-of-apps-discovery.ts enumerates depth-2 and exits 1 on a second nested
Application, so adding one forces a human to look before it can hide in here.
`ungovernedRequests` carries every Application no rung touches, with its measured
total, so the sums are over the whole tree and not over the subset we chose to
shrink. A directory in neither list fails the coverage check; a row naming a
directory that is gone fails it too. `null` means the chart could not be fetched
at its pinned version -- UNKNOWN, refused rather than counted as zero, unless
acknowledged in `acknowledgedUnmeasuredRequests` keyed by `<dir>@<pin>` so a
version bump invalidates the acknowledgement instead of inheriting it.
2026-08-21: that invalidation fired for real. `forgejo` was acknowledged as
`forgejo@9.0.6` ONLY because the pin was fictional and nothing could be pulled.
Correcting the pin to `17.1.5` moved the key, and the honest response was to
MEASURE it rather than re-key to `forgejo@17.1.5` -- re-keying would have
preserved a 'we cannot measure this' claim that had stopped being true, which is
an acknowledgement outliving its defect. Every total above moved by its 100m /
128Mi. `oz@1.4.5` stays: that pin is still fictional.

runnerEnvelope.measuredFreeDiskEvidence: READ, NOT DECLARED, and deliberately NOT the bound above. `runner-disk.ts --measure` on run 32585090483 reported / at 144.26 GiB with 77.06 GiB available on `ubuntu-24.04` and 99.02 GiB on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, after checkout and toolchain install; one filesystem, no /mnt, images on /var/lib/docker under /. A further 20.72 GiB (x64) / 4.52 GiB (arm) sits in preinstalled toolchains no k8s lane invokes. NOTHING PRICES AGAINST THIS FIELD. It is here so the measurement is first-class and citable while `freeDiskGib` stays where the tree's consumers put it -- `lane-partition.ts` prices every lane against `freeDiskGib - reservedDiskGib`, and raising it moves which Applications come out `oversize`. That conclusion should move as a deliberate decision alongside the partition work, not as a side effect of one agent reading `df`. PROPOSED CORRECTION, for a human to take or refuse: freeDiskGib 14 -> 70 (a conservative floor beneath both runners). MEASURED CONSEQUENCE of taking it, so the trade is visible: three assertions in lane-partition.test.ts flip -- `all applications together do NOT fit one runner`, `hindsight and vllm are the measured self-hosted case`, and the partition it packs. Those are conclusions about the tree, not test bugs, which is exactly why the field did not move on its own.
runnerEnvelope.reservationEvidence: THE CPU AND MEMORY HALVES are GitHub's published spec for a hosted `ubuntu-24.04` standard runner (4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM), checked by `--measure-runner`: run on the runner it reads /proc/cpuinfo and /proc/meminfo and CONVICTS when the real machine is smaller than this record claims. THE DISK HALF IS STILL THE VENDOR SPEC (14 GB free SSD) AND IS NOW KNOWN TO UNDERSTATE THE MACHINE BY MORE THAN 5x -- see `measuredFreeDiskGib` beside it for what two runners actually reported and why the bound did not move with it. `runner-disk.ts --check-envelope` convicts when a runner has LESS than this declares, so an understating bound makes that check weak rather than wrong: it still catches a machine smaller than 14 GiB and it no longer catches much else. That is the honest cost of leaving the field where its consumers put it. 16 GB is recorded as 15360Mi because GB is decimal and Kubernetes quantities are binary. THE RESERVED HALF is 1500m / 6144Mi and splits three ways. (1) ~950m / ~290Mi for the kind control plane and kube-system, which the scheduler subtracts from allocatable before any Application is placed: kubeadm's static-pod defaults (apiserver 250m, controller-manager 200m, scheduler 100m, etcd 100m/100Mi), coredns 2 x 100m/70Mi, kindnet 100m/50Mi. argo-cd 7.7.10 adds nothing -- rendered 2026-08-21, every component's `resources` is unset. (2) ~550m / ~1536Mi ESTIMATED for what lives outside the kind node's cgroup and which the scheduler therefore cannot see at all: the host OS, the Actions runner agent, dockerd/containerd, and the bun harness driving the run. kind imposes no memory limit on its node container, so the kubelet reports the HOST's capacity as the node's -- meaning this slice is real and invisible, and under-reserving it shows up as the runner OOMing rather than as a Pending pod. (3) the remaining ~4300Mi is UNRESERVED HEADROOM for BestEffort pods. 28 of the 45 Applications render pods that request nothing, so the scheduler will admit any number of them and this arithmetic will never see one. That headroom is the only thing standing between them and the kernel OOM killer, and it is the reason this budget is deliberately not tight.

resourceClaims.evidence: mimir-distributed 5.5.1 values.yaml default; our valuesObject does not set it. Rendered and counted 2026-08-21 with `helm template` against this Application's own valuesObject.
resourceClaims.consequence: Compaction working set. At 192Mi the compactor can only hold a smaller block set at a time; a tenant whose block set outgrows it stalls compaction and query performance degrades. Nothing is deleted -- the blocks stay in object storage uncompacted.

resourceClaims.evidence: mimir-distributed 5.5.1 values.yaml default; our valuesObject does not set it. Rendered and counted 2026-08-21 with `helm template` against this Application's own valuesObject.
resourceClaims.consequence: The distributor buffers incoming series before fan-out to ingesters. At 192Mi a write burst that would have been absorbed is instead pushed back on the client (429), and a burst larger than the buffer OOMKills the pod rather than queueing. Acceptable in CI, where write volume is a smoke test; NOT acceptable on metal, which is why `metal` keeps 512Mi.

resourceClaims.evidence: mimir-distributed 5.5.1 values.yaml; zoneAwareReplication.enabled=true over 3 zones and templates/_helpers.tpl:568 replicaPerZone = ceil(replicas/zones), so one `resources` key renders into 3 zone StatefulSets. Rendered and counted 2026-08-21 with `helm template` against this Application's own valuesObject.
resourceClaims.consequence: The ingester holds the in-flight head block in memory before shipping to object storage. 192Mi bounds how many active series one ingester can hold; past that it OOMKills and the series are re-replayed from the WAL on restart. Data already shipped to MinIO is unaffected. This value is multiplied by 3 zones.

resourceClaims.evidence: mimir-distributed 5.5.1 values.yaml default; our valuesObject does not set it. Rendered and counted 2026-08-21 with `helm template` against this Application's own valuesObject.

resourceClaims.evidence: mimir-distributed 5.5.1 values.yaml default; our valuesObject does not set it. Rendered and counted 2026-08-21 with `helm template` against this Application's own valuesObject.
resourceClaims.consequence: Query execution working set. Below the working set a large query is OOMKilled mid-flight and returns an error rather than a slow answer. Two replicas by chart default.

$comment_profiles: Order is smallest-first and is load-bearing: storage-profiles.ts refuses a
catalogue whose per-claim sizes are not monotonically non-decreasing along it.

`measured` sits between `standard` and `large` and is defined by a rule
rather than by a size: every claim with scheduledAtBringUp true takes
`standard`'s value, and every claim with scheduledAtBringUp false takes
`large`'s. It is therefore >= standard and <= large on every row, which is
why it slots in there without disturbing the monotonicity check.
It exists because those two sets answer different questions. The scheduled
set has to FIT — it provisions on a fresh sync, so it is bounded by what
Longhorn will place on the box that exists. The deferred set is a planning
CEILING that nothing applies, so shrinking it buys no headroom the cluster
ever spends; it only deletes a stated intent. Running plain `standard` would
have taken ollama and vllm from 200Gi to 48Gi and the arc model cache from
100Gi to 32Gi as a side effect of fitting a disk they never touch. That is a
product decision wearing an arithmetic costume, and it is not this rung's to

claims.consequence: RETENTION CUT, AND IT IS NOW AUTOMATIC — this row is where the `governors` mechanism came from. The Application sets `retention: 15d` beside this volume, which is a TIME bound that cannot see the disk, and kube-prometheus-stack 65.5.0 leaves `retentionSize` unset, so Prometheus applied no size bound at all: it fills the volume and the WAL wedges. This row used to say that anyone selecting a smaller rung "must also cut retention" and that the field was NOT rewritten by --apply. An instruction to remember is not a mechanism; the governor below is. `retentionSize` now moves in the same --apply pass as the size it bounds, so the two cannot land apart, and verifyProfileApplied goes red if the manifest drifts from either. What the cut still costs is real: at 32Gi you get 15 days OR ~24 GiB of blocks, whichever comes first, and nobody here has measured this cluster's ingest rate to say which binds.
claims.governorEvidence: kube-prometheus-stack 65.5.0 values.yaml:3732 ships prometheus.prometheusSpec.retentionSize: "" — UNSET, so Prometheus applies NO size-based retention and grows until the volume is full; retention: 15d is a TIME bound and cannot see the disk. The Prometheus CRD (crd-prometheuses.yaml:7656) defines retentionSize as "Maximum number of bytes used by the Prometheus data" and its pattern requires a B suffix, so 24Gi is INVALID here and 24GiB is the form. Both bounds are applied by Prometheus and whichever triggers first wins, so adding this cannot lengthen retention — it can only stop the disk filling. THE 75% FRACTION IS A BUDGET CHOICE, NOT A DERIVED REQUIREMENT: size-based retention deletes the oldest block only after the limit is crossed, so the volume needs room for the head block and the WAL on top of the retained set, and we have not measured this cluster's ingest rate to say how much. 75% is round, conservative, and stated as a choice rather than smuggled in as a minimum.
